CCTV Camera Frame & Video Ingestion Pipeline

datasource_health.name: Multimodal Late-Fusion & Quantile GBR Engine
datasource_health.notes: Calibrated on n=390 train / n=90 val records; evaluated on n=120 held-out chronological test records.

datasource_health.name: External Municipal Loop-Detector & RTSP Camera Stream
datasource_health.notes: Requires authorized RTSP/WebSocket endpoint and municipal TMC credentials.

evaluation_metrics.validation_methodology: Strict chronological split (65% Train [n=390], 15% Validation [n=90] for temperature scaling & conformal quantile interval calibration, 20% Held-Out Future Test [n=120]) with explicit target-leakage firewall.

dataset_manifest.environment_constraint_notice: Outbound internet access is disabled in the isolated VM environment. Accordingly, public external archives (US-Accidents, CADP, DAD, PeMS-Bay) are documented as reference schemas below, and the platform generates a reproducible, chronologically ordered 600-record Multimodal Traffic Incident & Network Benchmark (`incidents_multimodal_benchmark.csv`) paired with real OpenCV-analyzed CCTV imagery and video clips in `data/media/`.

datasets.name: Chennai Corridor Multimodal Traffic Incident & Recovery Benchmark (Local Active Dataset)
datasets.source: Generated deterministically via `backend/app/data_pipeline.py` (seed=42) on 14-node, 25-segment Greater Chennai corridor topology
target_labels: severity (4 ordinal operational classes: low, moderate, high, critical)
incident_clearance_minutes (Target A: physical roadway scene clearance duration)
network_recovery_minutes (Target B: full upstream queue dissipation & >=90% free-flow restoration)
datasets.data_quality_and_limitations: 8.0% of records intentionally omit visual features (`has_visual_modality=0`) to test explicit missing-modality handling without silent imputation. Durations follow physical LWR queue discharge dynamics with stochastic variance; must be retrained on municipal TMC logs before field dispatch.

datasets.name: US-Accidents (Countrywide Traffic Accident Dataset — Reference Schema)
datasets.source: Moosavi et al. (Sobhan Moosavi, Kaggle / OSU)
datasets.format: CSV (Structured incident metadata, weather, POI, start/end timestamps)
datasets.data_quality_and_limitations: Contains incident reporting and clearance timestamps + weather observations, but lacks CCTV visual frames and does not measure post-clearance road-network queue recovery time.

datasets.name: CADP (CCTV Traffic Accidents) & DAD (Dashcam Accident Dataset — Reference Schema)
datasets.source: Shah et al. (CADP) / Chan et al. (DAD)
datasets.format: MP4/JPEG Video Frames with Bounding Box & Temporal Accident Onset Annotations
datasets.data_quality_and_limitations: Provides visual collision evidence for computer-vision detection (Module B), but contains zero clearance duration or road-network recovery ground-truth timestamps.

datasets.name: Caltrans PeMS / METR-LA Loop Detector Telemetry (Reference Schema)
datasets.format: HDF5 / CSV Time-Series (5-minute speed, flow, occupancy sensor aggregates)
target_labels: Link speed recovery timestamp (when speed returns >= 90% free-flow)
datasets.data_quality_and_limitations: Required to observe true Target B (`network_recovery_minutes`) in production deployments.

network_impact.methodology_and_limitations: Road-network impact is computed on a 14-node, 25-directed-segment topological graph using Lighthill-Whitham-Richards (LWR) capacity-reduction queue propagation and Dijkstra shortest-time routing. Clearing the primary incident does not immediately restore upstream links; queue discharge continues until t = network_recovery_minutes. Detour travel times reflect modeled link states rather than live municipal loop-detector feeds unless connected to an active traffic management stream.
